associations.rationale: The formal type lifts an equivalence of factor modules at a fixed index to an equivalence of their inflations; it supports the classification but does not state it.
The formal type shows that equivalent inflated modules have equal factor indices under a nontriviality hypothesis, covering only the index-uniqueness component.
The formal type states that an inflation is simple iff its factor module is simple, a prerequisite for the claimed classification rather than the whole classification.
The formal type recovers a factor-module equivalence from an equivalence of inflations at the same index, supporting factor-isomorphism uniqueness without stating the full claim.
The formal type gives, from a simple product-ring module, an index with a simple idempotent range and an equivalence to its inflation; it states the existence direction only.
